column2: 中古英语 togedere ← 古英语 tōgædere（聚到一处），由 tō（到）＋ gædere（相聚）构成 ← 原始印欧语 *gʰedʰ-（合、聚）
column3: with each other, in one group or at one time
column5: They walked home together after class.|Mix the flour and butter together.
column6: in one place or one action rather than apart – 合在一处或一个动作里，不各行其是
column7: 一起：同处一地或同做一事|共同：几方一齐参与|一并：把几件事合到一处办

column2: 借自中古法语 toilette，是 toile（布）的指小形；本指理发修面时护衣的布，后引申指梳洗之所，19 世纪末在美国转指便所
column3: a bowl for waste, or the room containing it
column5: The toilet is at the end of the corridor.|He fixed the leaking toilet.
column6: the fixture and the small room built for relieving oneself – 供人如厕的那件器具与那间小屋
column7: 厕所：那间屋子|马桶：屋里那件承接之物

column2: 中古英语 token ← 古英语 tācn（记号、标志）← 原始日耳曼语 *taikną（指示物）← 原始印欧语 *deyḱ-（指出、示明）
column3: a small object used as a sign or in place of money
column5: Hand in the token to collect your coat.|She gave him a ring as a token of trust.
column6: a small thing that stands for a larger claim – 一件小东西，代表一份更大的凭据
column7: 凭证：凭它主张某项权利|象征：拿实物代表抽象之义|代币：在特定场所代替钱用的那种小圆片

column2: 中古英语 toll ← 古英语 toll（通行税）← 原始日耳曼语 *tullaz（所数之数、账目）← 原始印欧语 *del-（数、算）；与 tell、tale 同支
column3: a charge for using a road or bridge, or the number lost in a disaster
column5: You pay a toll to cross the bridge.|The death toll rose to forty.
column6: a count that must be reckoned before passing – 通过之前须先算清的那笔数
column7: 通行费：过路过桥要交的钱|伤亡人数：灾祸中清点出的那个数目|鸣响：钟一下一下敲，也是在计数

column2: 英语 tomate 的变体，借自西班牙语 tomate ← 纳瓦特尔语 tomatl ← 原始乌托-阿兹特克语 *toma-
column3: a soft round red fruit eaten in salads and sauces
column5: She sliced a tomato for the salad.|These tomatoes ripen late in the season.
column6: a soft round red fruit full of juice and seeds – 又红又软、多汁多籽的圆果
column7: 番茄：书面与市场上的通名|西红柿：北方口语的叫法

column2: 中古英语 tombe ← 古法语 tombe ← 拉丁语 tumba ← 希腊语 tymbos（坟丘）← 原始印欧语 *tewh₂-（隆起）；取代了古英语 þrūh
column3: a place built to hold a dead body
column5: They found the tomb sealed with stone.|Flowers lay at the foot of the tomb.
column6: a built chamber made to hold the dead – 造出来安放遗体的那个室
column7: 坟墓：安葬之处的通称|陵墓：规模大、多为贵者所建的那种

column2: 中古英语 tomorwe ← 古英语 tō morgne（在早晨），由 tō（在）＋ morgen（早晨）的与格构成
column3: on the day after today
column5: We leave for Rome tomorrow.|Tomorrow will be warmer than today.
column6: the day that comes next after this one – 紧接着这一天的下一天
column7: 明天：口语说法|明日：书面说法，义同

column2: 英语 ton 是 tun（大桶）的变体，受古法语 tonne（吨）影响；本以一桶酒的重量为准
column3: a unit of weight equal to about a thousand kilograms
column5: The lorry carries ten tons of gravel.|She has tons of work this week.
column6: a large fixed unit of weight, once a caskful – 一个大的定量重量单位，原以一桶为准
column7: 吨：计量重量的那个单位|大量：口语里借这个大单位说「很多」

column2: 中古英语 ton ← 拉丁语 tonus（音、调），或经古法语 ton 传入 ← 希腊语 tonos（张力、音高）← teino（拉伸）
column3: the quality of a sound, or the way something is said
column5: She answered in a sharp tone.|The walls are painted in warm tones.
column6: the particular quality that marks one sound or shade from another – 使一个声音或色泽区别于另一个的那种性质
column7: 音调：声音的高低与性质|语气：说话时透出的那种态度|色调：颜色的深浅倾向

column2: 中古英语 tonge ← 古英语 tunge ← 原始日耳曼语 *tungǭ（舌）← 原始印欧语 *dn̥ǵʰwéh₂s（舌）；与拉丁语 lingua 同源
column3: the soft movable part inside the mouth used for tasting and speaking
column5: He burned his tongue on the soup.|She speaks three tongues fluently.
column6: the soft movable organ in the mouth that shapes speech and taste – 口中那块能动的软肉，管说话也管辨味
column7: 舌：口中那个器官|语言：因说话靠它，故以它代指所说的话

column2: 中古英语 tonyght ← 古英语 tō niht（在这一夜），即 to ＋ night
column3: during the evening or night of today
column5: We are eating out tonight.|Tonight there will be frost.
column6: the night of the day one is now in – 眼下这一天的那个夜里
column7: 今夜：书面些的说法|今天晚上：口语说法，义同

column2: 中古英语 to（也、此外）← 古英语 tō（此外、也），是介词 tō 的副词用法
column3: also, or more than is wanted
column5: She wants to come too.|The soup is too salty.
column6: added on beyond what was there, sometimes beyond what suits – 在原有之外再添，添过了就成了过头
column7: 也：在已有的之外再加一个|太：超过合适的程度|过于：程度上越过了界

column2: 中古英语 toth ← 古英语 tōþ ← 原始日耳曼语 *tanþs ← 原始印欧语 *h₃dónts（牙）；与拉丁语 dens 同源
column3: one of the hard white parts in the mouth used for biting
column5: The dentist pulled out a back tooth.|Brush your teeth before bed.
column6: one of the hard white parts set in the jaw for biting – 长在颌上、用来咬的那种硬白小块
column7: 牙齿：日常通称|牙：单字说法，多用于复合词

column2: 中古英语 top ← 古英语 topp（顶、尖、簇）← 原始日耳曼语 *tuppaz（辫、末端），更早词源不明
column3: the highest part or surface of something
column5: Write your name at the top of the page.|She finished top of her class.
column6: the part with nothing above it – 上面再没有别的那一部分
column7: 顶部：整体最上那一片|顶端：最上那一个点|首位：排序里最前那一名

column2: 源自拉丁语 topica ← 希腊语 topikos（与处所有关的、与论题有关的）← topos（处所）
column3: the subject being talked or written about
column5: They changed the topic quickly.|Each essay covers one topic.
column6: the one matter that the talking keeps to – 说话所围绕的那一件事
column7: 话题：谈话所谈的那件事|题目：文章或讨论所立的那个题

column2: 中古英语 torche（大烛、点着的棍）← 古法语 torche（火把、扭成的草束），或出自通俗拉丁语 *torca（扭成之物）← 拉丁语 torqueō（扭、拧）
column3: a small electric lamp carried in the hand, or a burning stick
column5: Take a torch; the path is unlit.|Runners carried the torch through the city.
column6: a light one carries in the hand to see by – 手里提着照路的那个光源
column7: 电筒：装电池的那种手提灯|火把：点着的那种，本义在此

column2: 借自法语 torrent ← 意大利语 torrente ← 拉丁语 torrentem（奔涌的），是 torrēre（烤、灼）的现在分词
column3: a violent fast-moving stream, or a rush of something
column5: A torrent swept the bridge away.|He faced a torrent of questions.
column6: water moving so fast and full that nothing holds it – 水又急又满，什么也拦不住
column7: 洪流：来势极猛的大股水|湍流：流得急、翻卷不平的水|连串：把这股势头用到话或事上，一波接一波

column2: 中古英语 tossen（颠动、簸扬），更早词源不明；或出自古诺尔斯语，或为 tosen（撕扯）的变体
column3: to throw something lightly, or to move about restlessly
column5: She tossed the keys onto the table.|He tossed all night in the heat.
column6: sending something up with a light careless movement – 随手往上一送，不使大力
column7: 抛：轻轻往上或往前送出|掷：使些力气投出去|翻来覆去：身体不安地来回动，如同被颠着

column2: 中古英语 total ← 古法语 total ← 中世纪拉丁语 totalis ← 拉丁语 totus（全部的），totus 更早词源不明
column3: the whole amount, or complete and without exception
column5: The total came to ninety pounds.|It was a total failure.
column6: the whole taken together, with nothing left out – 全部合起来算，一样不漏
column7: 合计：各项加起来得出的数|总额：那个数所代表的金额|完全的：形容一件事到了彻底的程度

column2: 中古英语 touchen ← 古法语 tochier（触）← 通俗拉丁语 *tuccō（敲、碰）← 法兰克语 *tukkōn（碰、拉）← 原始印欧语 *dewk-（牵、拉）
column3: to put a hand or finger on something
column5: Do not touch the wet paint.|Her story touched everyone present.
column6: bringing one surface into contact with another – 让一个表面与另一个挨上
column7: 触摸：手放上去感觉|碰到：与某物发生接触|触动：把这一碰用到人心上，指使人动情

column2: 中古英语 tough ← 古英语 tōh（坚韧的、黏的）← 原始日耳曼语 *tanhuz（黏牢的、韧的）← 原始印欧语 *denḱ-（咬）
column3: hard to break or cut, or hard to bear
column5: The meat was tough and dry.|They went through a tough winter.
column6: holding together under strain instead of giving way – 受力时抱住不散，不肯让开
column7: 坚韧的：材料受折不断|艰难的：处境使人难熬|强硬的：态度硬，不肯松口

column2: 源自古法语 tour／tourn（一圈），出自动词 torner（转）← 拉丁语 tornare（车削、旋转）
column3: a journey visiting several places and returning
column5: They went on a tour of the lakes.|The band starts its tour in May.
column6: a round trip that takes in several places and comes back – 绕一圈，走过几处再回来
column7: 旅行：为游览而走的那一趟|巡演：演出团体逐地演出的那一圈|游览：到一处逐点看过

column2: 由 tour ＋ -ist 构成；tour 一支 ← 古法语 tour（一圈）← 拉丁语 tornare（旋转）
column3: a person travelling for pleasure
column5: Tourists crowded the old square.|The town lives on tourists in summer.
column6: one who travels to see places for pleasure – 为看景取乐而出行的人
column7: 观光者：以看景为主的那种旅人|旅游者：泛指出门游玩的人

column2: 中古英语 towen ← 古英语 togian（拖）← 原始日耳曼语 *tugōną（拉、拽）← 原始印欧语 *dewk-（牵、拉）
column3: to pull a vehicle along behind another
column5: A truck towed the broken car away.|They towed the barge upriver.
column6: pulling something along behind by a rope or bar – 用绳或杆把东西挂在后面拉着走
column7: 拖：在后面拉着行进|牵引：以机械之力拉动，多用于车船

column2: 中古英语 toward ← 古英语 tōweard，即 to ＋ -ward（朝…方向）
column3: in the direction of, or in relation to
column5: She walked toward the gate.|His attitude toward the plan has changed.
column6: facing or moving in the direction of something – 面朝或行向某处
column7: 朝向：动作或位置对着某方|接近：时间或数量上快到某点|对于：把这个「朝向」用到态度上

column2: 中古英语 towayle ← 古法语 toaille（毛巾）／中世纪拉丁语 toallia ← 法兰克语 *þwahilu（布）← 原始日耳曼语 *þwahaną（洗）
column3: a piece of cloth used for drying
column5: He dried his hands on a towel.|Hang the wet towel on the rail.
column6: a cloth that takes up water from what it wipes – 一块布，把擦过之处的水吸走
column7: 毛巾：日常用来擦身擦手的那种布|擦手布：专供擦手的那一种

column2: 中古英语 tour ← 古英语 tūr 与古法语 tour，两支同出拉丁语 turris（塔）← 希腊语 tyrsis；取代了中古英语 stepel
column3: a tall narrow building or part of a building
column5: A stone tower stood above the walls.|Cliffs tower over the beach.
column6: a structure built far higher than it is wide – 造得远比宽度高的那种建筑
column7: 塔：独立的那种高耸建筑|高楼：楼房中特别高的那些|高耸：把这个形状当动作说，指远高于周围

column2: 中古英语 toun ← 古英语 tūn（围地、庄院）← 原始日耳曼语 *tūną（篱、围地）；德语 Zaun（篱）与之同源
column3: a place with houses and shops, larger than a village
column5: She grew up in a small town.|The town has one cinema.
column6: a settlement bigger than a village but short of a city – 比村大、够不上城的那种聚居地
column7: 镇：行政或习惯上称镇的那种地方|城镇：连着城一起说的通称

column2: 借自法语 toxique ← 晚期拉丁语 toxicus（有毒的）← 拉丁语 toxicum（毒）← 希腊语 toxikon（涂在箭上的毒）← toxon（弓）
column3: containing poison, or very harmful
column5: The fumes are highly toxic.|He left a toxic workplace.
column6: carrying something that harms whatever takes it in – 带着能害人的东西，谁碰上谁受损
column7: 有毒的：含毒，入体致害|有害的：把这层推开，指对人对事都不好

column2: 中古英语 toye（嬉戏、玩意），或出自中古荷兰语 tuyg（家伙、器具）← 原始日耳曼语 *teugą（所拉之物、器具）← 原始印欧语 *dewk-（拉）
column3: an object made for children to play with
column5: The floor was covered with toys.|He treats the car as a toy.
column6: a thing made only to be played with – 专为玩而做的东西
column7: 玩具：给孩子玩的那些器物|玩物：被当作消遣之物的东西，多含贬义
